name: Sporecap
behaviour: Stands still among the trees and looks like any mushroom, then gets up and waddles off. Harmless at a distance. Stand next to it and it ducks under its cap, shivers, then jumps and throws a ring of spores: no damage, but you walk slowly for a few seconds. Agents learn to harvest it from two tiles away, or to wait until it has puffed.

stats.drops: mushroom, spores (plant them to grow more)

name: Hopper
where: marsh, pond edges, wet fields after rain
behaviour: Sits by the water and croaks. It moves only in hops, one tile at a time, with a pause between. It does not bite: its tongue snatches the item you hold (or one crop from a field) from two tiles away, and it hops off with it. Catch it within a few seconds and it drops what it took.

stats.speed: a tile per hop, faster than you in bursts

name: Burrow
where: soft ground: meadows, fields, gardens. Never under stone or paths
behaviour: A line of molehills coming your way is all you see. It tunnels under fences and walls, eats one root crop, and leaves. Under your feet it bursts out and knocks you back a tile (small damage). It can only be hit while it is out of the ground; a paved or stone floor keeps it away, so it teaches agents to pave what they care about.

stats.drops: hide; its molehills leave a seed or a pebble

name: Hush
where: perches in tall trees at the forest edge
behaviour: By day it sleeps in a tree and is only a pair of eyes. At night it glides over fences and water, silent, and goes for small animals left outside: a chicken or chick in the open is carried off. It holds still in the air before it drops, so a player or agent standing by the coop can hit it then. It never attacks people; a roof or a lit torch near the coop keeps it away.

name: Cairn
behaviour: Sleeps as a pile of mossy stones beside the ore it guards. Mine next to it and it stands up. It is slow and easy to outwalk, but tools barely scratch it. It raises both fists for more than half a second, then slams: everything within one tile is hurt and thrown back. While its fists are down it takes full damage. Leave its ore alone and it sits back down. One per mountain, never more.
